name: Tiny home community
summary: A tiny home community is priced per pad: utility stubs (water, sewer, 50-100A electric), a foundation or pier/parking pad, roads, landscaping and a share of a community building, with the home itself either owner-supplied (tiny house on wheels) or developer-supplied (optional line item). Published budgets are almost all supportive/transitional villages (Quixote Village WA, Los Angeles tiny home villages), so the market-rate default is derived from those and from the RV park per-site evidence. Confidence low-medium.

typicalSize.method: Quixote Village has 30 cottages (t1: $3.05M total / $101,567 per unit = 30); Los Angeles villages averaged 1,217 beds / 9 villages (~135 beds, many double-occupancy shelters) (t2). Market-rate tiny home communities are typically 20-60 pads; mid 35.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Quixote Village: 30 cottages on 'just over 2 acres' (t3) = ~14/acre with a community building. Market-rate communities give larger yards; mid 12.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Supportive villages provide little parking; market-rate communities typically one space per pad plus guest parking. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per-pad site and shared infrastructure, excluding the home. (1) Quixote Village (2013, WA): paid cost ~$88k/unit incl. soft costs and road improvements, minus ~$19k cottage = ~$69k; less ~15% soft = ~$59k hard per pad (t1). (2) Los Angeles tiny home villages (2021-22): average construction $42,344 per bed incl. ~$8.3k Pallet shelter (Chandler: $299,000/36) = ~$34k infrastructure per bed (t2). (3) Full-hookup RV site: ~$42k mid (rv-park-resort default; OH Weekly $30k-$40k per site all-in, rv e8). Mid $45k = RV-site infrastructure plus pier/parking pad and larger landscaped lot, consistent with the midpoint of (1) and (2). Low $20k = rural community with gravel roads and minimal common building; high $90k = urban infill with paved roads, concrete foundations and full community building. Evidence years 2013-2024, not escalated by hand.

scope.notes: Per-pad contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P: grading, roads, parking, on-site water/sewer/electric distribution and stubs to each pad, pad/foundation prep, landscaping and a share of the community building. Excludes the tiny home itself (optional line item), land, soft costs, off-site utilities, tap/impact fees.

systemSplit.method: Adapted from the RV park split (OH Weekly itemization, rv e8): concrete raised to 0.08 for pier/slab pads, electrical raised to 0.14 for 100A residential services, utilities to 0.17 (permanent residential-grade laterals), roads/paving/landscape 0.26, community building (03-23 share) ~0.18, general conditions 0.08.

lineItems.name: Per-pad utility connection (water, sewer lateral, 50-100A electric pedestal/meter)

cost.method: RV park per-site sewer ($2.5k) + water ($2.4k) + electrical ($4.0k) = $8.9k (rv e8/e9), rounded to $9k; high for individual 100-200A meters and deeper laterals.

lineItems.name: Foundation / pier pad and skirting for tiny home

cost.method: Bob Vila: foundation for a tiny home ~$5,000-$8,000 or more (t4); low = gravel pad with piers for a THOW.

lineItems.name: Community building (kitchen, laundry, restrooms/showers, gathering room)

cost.method: Quixote Village included a community building with kitchen and showers within its $3.05M total (t1, not broken out). Sized as 1,500-3,000 SF at ~$250-$300/SF; cross-check: SD comfort station $705k (rv e17). Judgment.

lineItems.notes: Essential where homes lack full plumbing (supportive villages); optional amenity for market-rate communities.

lineItems.name: Developer-supplied tiny home (150-400 SF, delivered and set)

cost.method: Bob Vila: typical tiny house $30,000-$60,000, national average $45,000 (t4). Quixote cottages ~$19k (2013, no plumbing) and LIHI shelter houses $4.5k materials (t5) are shelter-grade floors, not used for the range. High = premium builder units.

lineItems.notes: Switch on for for-sale or rental communities where the developer supplies the homes.

cost.method: OH Weekly: small RV parks have done entire septic for ~$100k (rv e14); tiny homes generate year-round residential flows, so mid set at $200k for ~35 pads. Judgment.
Same basis as rv-park-resort interior-roads (OH Weekly paving $3.6k/site, rv e8) with ~35 LF per pad; high = curb, sidewalk and storm.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Community building furnishings, laundry machines, mailboxes, site furniture spread per pad. Judgment.

pctOfHard.method: Judgment: design/engineering ~8%, entitlements (rezoning/PUD or park licensing), surveys, permits and legal ~5-8%, developer overhead. Los Angeles supportive villages reportedly carried large permit/design/management costs relative to construction (not verified in this session). Mid 16%.

softCosts.notes: Zoning approvals for tiny home parks are often discretionary; budget extra entitlement time.

design.method: Judgment; code path (RV park vs. manufactured home park vs. subdivision) changes infrastructure requirements.

hard.method: Judgment, consistent with RV park norms.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min = rural gravel community with low soft costs; max = Quixote Village total $101,567/unit incl. donated land/services (t1, 2013) escalated, or LA high village $65,783/bed (t2) plus soft costs. Excludes the home unless the optional line is on.

source.title: Quixote Village 5-Year Report (Department of Commerce transmittal to legislators)
source.publisher: Washington State Department of Commerce / Quixote Communities

evidence.quote: Cost per unit, not including the value of donated land and services: Nearly $88,000 ... Cost for each cottage, not including shared facilities or land: About $19,000
evidence.scopeNotes: Total development $3.05M incl. infrastructure, materials, labor, community building, permits, fees, required road improvements, donated land and services; $101,567/unit incl. donated land (~$333k) and services. Opened December 2013. Supportive housing for formerly homeless adults; cottages without plumbing (shared community building).

source.title: What Are the Costs of Building Tiny Home Villages to Decrease Homelessness?

evidence.quote: The average construction cost per bed is $42,344. ... Construction costs per bed range from $32,712 to $65,783.
evidence.scopeNotes: Nine LA city villages (1,217 beds) as of March 2022; includes pre-planning, infrastructure (electricity, sanitation, water, plumbing), Pallet shelters and hygiene trailers. Mostly pre-construction estimates. Line items: Pallet shelters at Chandler Blvd $299,000 for 36; hygiene trailers $112,000.

source.title: Quixote Village 5-Year Report (Department of Commerce transmittal to legislators)
source.publisher: Washington State Department of Commerce / Quixote Communities

evidence.quote: Quixote Village occupies just over 2 acres
evidence.scopeNotes: 30 cottages (derived from $3.05M / $101,567) plus community building => ~14 units per acre.

source.title: How Much Does a Tiny House Cost?

evidence.quote: The typical range for the cost of a tiny house is $30,000 to $60,000, with a national average of $45,000.
evidence.scopeNotes: Consumer cost guide (last modified 2023-09-19). Same page: 'Constructing a foundation for a tiny home will vary in cost from around $5,000 to $8,000 or more'; municipal sewer connection fees '$500 to $20,000'.

evidence.quote: The cost of materials for a tiny house is $4,500.
evidence.scopeNotes: Approximately 8 x 12 ft shelter with electricity, light, insulation and heater; volunteer-built; emergency shelter grade. Page undated; footer shows (c) 2023, so dataYear 2023 assumed.

openQuestions: Need market-rate (non-shelter) tiny home community budgets - e.g., Community First! Village (Austin) phase budgets, Habitat or land-trust tiny home projects - none could be retrieved in this session.
Per-pad utility stub cost assumes RV-park-like infrastructure; jurisdictions treating tiny homes as dwellings may require individual meters and fire hydrant spacing that raise cost.
Web search budget was exhausted mid-session; Community First! Village and Seattle/Portland village budgets were not verified.
